ChatCompletionChunk.description:
One `data:` event of a streamed completion (SSE).

The stream ends with `data: [DONE]`. A chunk carrying `usage` (and
`cost_usd` when the gateway computed it) always comes before `[DONE]`.
A stream the provider breaks off after its first chunk ends instead with
`data: {"error": {"message", "type": "server_error", "code":
"stream_interrupted"}}`, then `data: [DONE]`.

ErrorResponse.description:
FastAPI's error body. Upstream timeouts (503) add `retry_after` and a
Retry-After header, as does an exhausted provider quota (429) when the
provider gave a delay; a failing CLI provider (502) adds its exit details
for the admin only. A chat model no provider knows (404) adds `code` and
`hint`. A chat whose candidate providers all stayed at their concurrency
cap, or had too many requests already waiting (503), adds `code`
providers_busy, `retry_after` and Retry-After; one
the global chat cap kept waiting for a slot (503) adds `code`
server_busy, `retry_after` and Retry-After; one whose session's previous
turn was still being answered when its wait ended, or with too many turns
already waiting (503), adds `code`
session_busy, `retry_after` and Retry-After. A
chat model of a provider the admin turned off (503) adds `code`
provider_disabled and `hint`, without Retry-After. A key with a monthly
budget, while usage cannot be recorded (503), gets `code`
usage_unavailable, `retry_after` and Retry-After. A chat request only
CLI subscription routes could serve, asking for what they cannot serve
(400), adds `code` unsupported_on_cli, `unsupported` (the refused fields)
and `hint`. A prompt a CLI subscription route finds too long (400) adds
`code` context_length_exceeded, `error_ref`, `provider_name` and
`model_id`. A model a CLI subscription route's account plan does not serve
(400) adds `code` model_not_supported_by_subscription, `hint`,
`error_ref`, `provider_name` and `model_id`. A chat the provider failed
(400 rejected request, 401 or 403 provider credentials, 502, a 503
timeout) adds `error_ref`; a client key's `detail` is then a sentence
written by the gateway, never the provider's or the exception's text.

code.description: Stable reason for programs, when the route gives one: invalid_request (chat, 400; messages, a role or an output cap no provider can answer), unsupported_on_cli (chat, 400), context_length_exceeded (chat, 400), cli_tool_call_invalid (chat, 502; tools emulated on a CLI route and the model answered off the protocol: do not retry), model_not_supported_by_subscription (chat, 400), model_not_found (chat, 404), providers_busy (chat, 503), server_busy (chat and preflight, 503; also a preflight item's error), session_busy (chat, 503), provider_disabled (chat, 503), provider_timeout (chat, 503; a provider gave no answer in time), provider_sandbox_unavailable (chat, 503; the agy provider's sandbox could not start, so agy was not run), quota_exhausted (chat, 429; the provider's subscription or API quota is exhausted), forbidden_model (chat, 403; the key may not use the model), usage_unavailable (a key with a monthly budget while usage cannot be recorded: chat, preflight, embeddings and decisions, 503).
code.title: Code

error_ref.description: Reference of the gateway log entry that holds the error's own text (search the log for ref=<error_ref>).
error_ref.title: Error Ref

hint.description: What to do next, when the gateway knows.
hint.title: Hint

unsupported.description: With code unsupported_on_cli: the request fields a CLI subscription route cannot serve (tools, tool_choice, functions, function_call, response_format, content:<part type>).
unsupported.title: Unsupported

400.description: Invalid request; nothing was billed. code unsupported_on_cli: only CLI subscription routes (subprocess providers) serve the model and the request asks for what they cannot serve: tools, a tool_choice other than none or auto, functions, a function_call other than none or auto, a response_format other than text, or a content part other than text; unsupported lists them, hint says what to send; nothing was called. code context_length_exceeded: a CLI subscription route found the prompt too long for the model's context; no other provider was tried. code model_not_supported_by_subscription: the account plan a CLI subscription route is signed in with does not serve the model (codex with a ChatGPT account); hint says what to do, no other provider was tried. code invalid_request (BUG-121): messages missing or invalid, a message role other than system, developer, user, assistant, tool or function (detail names it, cut to 40 characters), or a max_tokens or max_completion_tokens that is not a whole number from 1 to 262144 (detail names the field); for every caller, the admin key included, before the budget hold; nothing was called. Without code: a body that is not valid JSON or not a JSON object, a model that is not a string or is removed, a session_id that is a list or an object, a decision model (use /v1/decisions), or a request an HTTP provider rejected (context too long, parameters; error_ref): after the other candidates were tried, whether the request asked for a stream or not (PLU-26), or at once when the stream had already begun.

401.description: Missing or invalid API key; or the provider's own credentials could not be used (a CLI login expired, an OAuth token refused) on the last provider tried: error_ref, nothing was called on that provider.

402.description: The key has a monthly budget and the model no known price; nothing was called.

403.description: The key may not use this model (code forbidden_model); or the provider's own credentials could not be used on the last provider tried (a Copilot licence missing, for example): error_ref, nothing was called on that provider.

404.description: No provider knows the model: no provider ID prefixes it, no provider lists it, and every active provider has a model list. Or the model ID selects CLI subscription routes only (claude, codex, gemini, agy) and none serves it: the name starts with - or holds a space, a line break or a control character, or, for a route that lists models, is not in its catalogue (listed models, default model, family aliases, the CLI's own aliases); for every caller, the admin key included, and the detail is generic. code is model_not_found, hint says what to send; nothing was called.

413.description: Request body larger than MAX_BODY_BYTES (10 MB by default).

429.description: Rate limit or monthly spending limit exceeded, or this call's estimated cost does not fit in what the budget has left once the calls in progress are counted (nothing was called), or the quota of the last provider tried is exhausted (code quota_exhausted; retry_after and Retry-After when it gives a delay).

502.description: The provider failed or answered with an error (error_ref). code cli_tool_call_invalid: tools were emulated as text on a CLI subscription route (PLUGBOARD_CLI_TOOLS_EMULATION=1 and allow_cli_tools on the key) and the model's answer was not one protocol object, called a tool not declared (or not the one tool_choice names), gave arguments that do not match the tool's parameters, made several calls with parallel_tool_calls false, or no call when one was required; detail gives the reason (and the tool name), error_ref the log entry; header x-should-retry: false; no other provider was tried, nothing was billed.

503.description: Provider timeout (code provider_timeout, retry_after), the agy provider's sandbox unable to start, agy not run (code provider_sandbox_unavailable, no Retry-After), the global cap of concurrent chat requests full for the whole wait (code server_busy, Retry-After 5), the previous turn of the request's session still answered when its wait ended, or too many of its turns already waiting (code session_busy, Retry-After 5), every candidate provider at its concurrency cap, or with too many requests already waiting for it (code providers_busy, Retry-After 5), or the model belongs to a provider the admin turned off (code provider_disabled, hint, no Retry-After), or the key has a monthly budget and usage cannot be recorded (code usage_unavailable, Retry-After 30); nothing was called.

routes.description:
Identities listed in PLUGBOARD_EMBEDDING_MODELS this key may use.

Unregistered owners and identities the key may not use are left out.
``available`` says whether the route resolves (owner registered, active,
loopback local engine); it does not probe the engine. ``dimensions`` is
known once a call was served since the last restart, else null.
routes.name: list_embedding_models

client_routes.description:
Smoke-test a batch of provider+model pairs before a long benchmark.

Each ping goes through the chat admission checks (allowed_models, budget,
a provider that is not turned off, a model some provider knows, known
price, rpm) and is billed like a chat call. The batch holds one slot of
the global cap, given back while a ping waits for a full provider and
taken back right before a provider is called (BUG-77, PLU-51): a pair it
cannot ping for want of a slot answers ``server_busy``. Errors are closed codes, never the
provider's text.
client_routes.name: preflight

client_routes.description: List all models enriched with benchmarks, capabilities, and metadata.
client_routes.name: models_with_benchmarks

client_routes.description: Get detailed info for a specific model: benchmarks, capabilities, best_for.
client_routes.name: model_info

client_routes.description:
Liveness (PLU-31): always 200 while the process answers. Public, so it
shows the status and the version only and reads no file; the provider
list is on the admin `GET /providers`, the auth posture on
`GET /health/ready`.
client_routes.name: health

client_routes.description:
Readiness (PLU-31): 200 when this instance can serve requests, 503
otherwise. Public: a load balancer reads the status code with no key.

The body is ``ready`` and ``version``; ``checks`` (generic states: which
check failed, the client auth posture) is added for a valid key only
(PLU-75): an active client key, the admin key (no TOTP: a read of
generic states) or an admin session, a person's session included; a
bare personal key (``pba_``), even with its code, gets no checks
(PB-AUTH-01). A wrong, forged or revoked key is
not refused here: it gets the same body as no key. With both API_KEY and
ADMIN_KEY empty every route is open (loopback only), so are the checks.
client_routes.name: health_ready

client_routes.description:
Detailed health check — probes every active provider.

Uses the same probe as the dashboard Ping (health_probe.probe_provider):
CLI providers are checked through their binary, local servers through
the URL they really serve, and the provider's credentials are sent.
client_routes.name: health_detailed

client_routes.description:
Chat calls in flight and the last results (PLU-13).

The admin sees every call with its provider; a client key sees its own
calls only, without routing details.
client_routes.name: inflight_me

client_routes.description: Every chat call in flight and the last results, with routing details.
client_routes.name: inflight_admin

client_routes.description: List the calling client's own keys (masked).
client_routes.name: client_keys
